fields.description_1:
Modern Image Manager brings WordPress media tasks into one admin workflow, which is useful but also risky. Editing metadata is simple compared with renaming files, importing CSV changes or deleting attachments, because those actions can affect URLs and references across the site. Large media libraries add another problem: a tool cannot safely load every item into memory at once.

The plugin therefore needed strict validation, bounded scans and conservative file handling around the features that can change media. Exports also had to be safe for spreadsheet use, while deletion should respect normal WordPress behaviour. The portfolio story needed to explain these boundaries instead of presenting cleanup as harmless automation. The challenge was to make media maintenance practical without hiding the operational risks behind an interface.
fields.description_2:
I built Modern Image Manager as a WordPress admin interface for metadata editing, CSV import and export, usage scanning and ZIP exports. Requests are validated before higher-risk actions run, and filename changes preserve the current extension. Metadata is saved only after a requested rename succeeds, preventing a failed file operation from leaving a partial update.

Large media scans run in batches rather than loading the whole library into memory. CSV exports protect against spreadsheet formula injection, and import, export and ZIP actions use capability and nonce checks. Attachment deletion follows normal WordPress media behaviour instead of forcing permanent removal. The portfolio case now explains the practical media workflow together with the safeguards that make bulk and file-level operations reviewable.

fields.description_1:
ACF Page Text Manager addresses a WordPress editing problem created when page text lives across core fields, ACF, SEO plugins and media metadata. Reviewing content one screen at a time is slow, but bulk spreadsheets introduce their own risks when unsupported fields or media instructions are included. The plugin needed one focused editing surface without becoming an unrestricted migration system.

Import and export also had to handle temporary files carefully, discover supported ACF fields dynamically and keep physical media renames behind an explicit extra step. Uninstall behaviour should remove plugin-owned state without deleting editorial content. The portfolio story needed to show both the productivity gain and these limits. The challenge was to centralise supported text work while keeping bulk writes, file handling and cleanup predictable.
fields.description_2:
I built ACF Page Text Manager around one WordPress admin screen for supported core fields, ACF text, SEO metadata and image text. Editors can update values inline or move selected content through CSV and XLSX workflows, with validation before imported data is processed. Supported ACF fields are discovered dynamically instead of being hard-coded for one website.

Temporary uploads are bounded and cleaned after processing. Physical filename changes remain an explicit opt-in path with additional confirmation, including a separate flag for command-line imports. The plugin checks ACF availability and limits uninstall cleanup to its own settings and temporary state. The portfolio case now describes a structured editorial workflow that improves reviewability without treating bulk content or media changes as unrestricted writes.

fields.description_1:
Spring architecten needs a portfolio that lets the work establish credibility before visitors read a long explanation of the studio. Prospective clients often start with project type, visual character and relevance. If service and company text comes first, the strongest evidence can be pushed behind generic messaging.

The website therefore needed to make projects easy to explore while keeping studio context and enquiry routes close enough to support the next decision. Images had to remain important on mobile without creating an endless visual stream. The portfolio story also had to avoid claiming design outcomes or client results that are not documented. The challenge was to organise architecture as evidence: show the work, explain enough context and give a prospective client a clear path to conversation.
fields.description_2:
I structured Spring architecten around project imagery and the information that helps a prospective client understand each piece of work. Projects come forward first, with architectural context and studio information supporting the visual evidence rather than competing with it. This lets visitors explore relevance before they are asked to make contact.

Enquiry actions appear after meaningful project or studio context, and the mobile layout keeps imagery, descriptions and next steps in a controlled order. I used concise headings so the portfolio remains easy to scan without reducing every project to the same formula. The case description stays focused on presentation and information architecture instead of invented outcomes. It now shows how WordPress can support an architecture portfolio where real work carries the story.

fields.description_1:
SEO Image Assistant for Shutterstock connects stock-image research with the WordPress page where an image may eventually be used. That creates more responsibility than a simple search box: OAuth credentials, licensing status, file validation and ACF assignments all sit in the same workflow. An asset can be visually suitable without being licensed or appropriate for the target field.

The plugin therefore needed clear separation between search, review, licensing, download and assignment. It also had to avoid rescanning the full media library whenever used-image context was needed. The portfolio story could not claim that a stock image automatically improves SEO. The challenge was to make page-aware image research efficient while keeping licensing, permissions, file safety and recovery visible before WordPress content is changed.
fields.description_2:
I built SEO Image Assistant for Shutterstock as a page-aware WordPress workflow that begins with keyword or page context and ends with a reviewed image assignment. OAuth connects the service, while search and suggestion queues let administrators inspect assets before licensing. Supported ACF image fields can then be mapped to the selected page context.

Licensed downloads are checked for allowed MIME type and file-size limits before import, and successful items from partial licensing responses remain recoverable. REST actions are capability-gated, while a stored used-ID index avoids scanning every attachment for each search. Uninstall data removal stays disabled by default. The portfolio case now explains controlled image research and licensing boundaries without suggesting that stock selection itself guarantees search visibility.

fields.description_1:
Dcaschoonmaak needs to help households and businesses identify the right cleaning service without reading every service page. Needs vary by property, frequency and situation, so clear service categories are more useful than broad promises. Trust should support the choice, not replace it.

The website therefore needed a simple route from the type of cleaning to relevant details and an enquiry. Coverage information also had to remain clear when location matters. On mobile, service cards and contact actions needed to stay easy to reach. The portfolio story had to avoid claims about guaranteed results, speed or customer satisfaction that were not independently measured. The challenge was to make a practical cleaning offer easy to understand while keeping each enquiry specific to the property and need.
fields.description_2:
I organised Dcaschoonmaak around the cleaning needs visitors are likely to recognize first. Separate service routes explain what each type of work covers, while practical and trust information appears where it helps someone decide whether the service fits. This reduces the need to browse unrelated sections before making contact.

Enquiry actions stay close to the relevant service, and coverage details are presented as practical context rather than broad availability promises. On smaller screens, service choices, supporting information and contact routes keep a compact order. I avoided claims about guaranteed outcomes or cleaning speed because those depend on the property and assignment. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress supports a straightforward service journey from cleaning need to a better-informed enquiry.
